Warcraft's Anniversary (or WoW's Anniversary) is an event celebrated in November with the dates of the 15th that marks the release of the first game and the 24th that marks the release of World of Warcraft. Logging in during an anniversary rewards a special achievement and gives a unique buff to experience and reputation earned for the duration of the event.

Warcraft III: Reforged is a remaster of Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. It was first announced at BlizzCon 2018 and was released on January 28 and 29, 2020. It will support graphics up to 4k and feature a revamped UI. The game is developed by the same team that did . It utilizes an upgraded version of the original game engine, in order to preserve mod functionality from the original game. Its graphics engine however has been completely overhauled. Reforged is available in two versions: the Standard Edition and the Spoils of War Edition. The game became available on the PC Game Pass on June 30th, 2025.
The Warcraft III: Reforged Spoils of War Edition includes a full digital copy of Warcraft III: Reforged along with in-game rewards for other Blizzard games.

The Warcraft III Battle Platform was a tournament platform for Warcraft III that was developed by . It used the Warcraft III client to watch real-time live tournaments or to play against players while allowing other players to view the battle. The platform was shutdown on 24 January 2023 due to the license agreement expiring that day with Blizzard Entertainment and NetEase unable to come to an agreement on renewing it.

Warcraft: Guardians of Azeroth is a fan-made mod for the game. The point of the mod is to let you experience the geopolitical world of Azeroth on a whole new scale, featuring game mechanics never used before in the series. For example, you could choose to play as Othmar Garithos, become king of the Stratholme region, ally with the Church of the Holy Light and eventually launch an assault on Kalimdor to burn Nordrassil down. As an orc leader, you could decide to create your own Horde and invite the centaur in it, while fighting randomized Scourge and Burning Legion invasions. In addition to the Single Player Campaign, Warcraft: Orcs & Humans supports head-to-head play against a human opponent over a modem, serial link, and IPX networks, and works cross-platform with both the IBM-PC and Macintosh versions. It is also possible to play one-off games against a computer-controlled opponent using the Custom Game option from the game menu.

Warcraft: Guardians of Azeroth 2 (or "Guardians of Azeroth Reforged") is a fan-made mod for the game. It is a sequel to Warcraft: Guardians of Azeroth, by the same developing team. Like its predecessor, "GOA2" lets the player experience the world of Azeroth through a geopolitical lense. One can choose to play as major characters of the franchise, as one of the many randomly-generated rulers, or even to create their own. The mod was first announced in September 13, 2020 and an Alpha version was released on March 20, 2023.

The First War was an intended bonus campaign for Warcraft III: Reforged, depicting an updated version of the events of the First War, originally shown in Warcraft: Orcs & Humans. It would have had hero-centric gameplay and storytelling. Though the campaign was never created, some of its design docs were released in 2023 by game designer David Fried on . This page is a transcription of these design docs.

If he is not there, there will be three dwarf guards instead. Unlike most of the other demon dogs in Blackrock Depths, Verek is *not* particularly sensitive to stealthed characters. "Warcraft Suite" is a medley of Warcraft III and World of Warcraft pieces composed by Jason Hayes and orchestrated by Benoit Grey for the concert series, including sections from "Legends of Azeroth," "Seasons of War," and "A Call to Arms." Live performances were accompanied by a music video cut together from Warcraft III cinematics and World of Warcraft's opening cutscene. A performance of the medley by the Slovak National Symphony Orchestra appears on Video Games Live, vol. 1, released on July 22, 2008.

"Warcraft Montage" is a medley of Warcraft III and World of Warcraft pieces composed by Jason Hayes and orchestrated by Benoit Grey for the concert series, including sections from "Legends of Azeroth," "Seasons of War," and "A Call to Arms." Live performances are accompanied by a music video cut together from Warcraft III cinematics and World of Warcraft's opening cutscene. A performance of the medley by the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra appears on Video Games Live: Level 2, released on October 19, 2010, and was also featured in a PBS special that first aired on July 31, 2010.

The six Warden Towers are currently contested areas throughout the Broken Isles. Each location has a chance to spawn a PvP World Quest. Both the Gilneas Brigade and the Forsaken Queensguard are interested in controlling these towers. While in the subzone the player has access to honor talents. Two more unnamed towers that are not contested by the two factions, and instead serve as max-level PvE locations, exist on the Isle of the Watchers in southern Azsuna. The one on the southern tip of Isle of the Watchers has been taken over by felsworn Illidari with Lysanis Shadesoul as their commander. The northern tower has Jade Darkhaven as the commander.

This evolution guide serves as an archive of anecdotes, trivia, and other interesting facts about the several game design shifts that Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos had during its development stage. Warcraft III was a huge step up for Blizzard Entertainment: it was their first 3D game, the first time they were developing a game concurrently alongside other medias like novels and TTRPG's, their previous Warcraft game had just been canceled, and they had very huge ambitions about shaking up the world of strategy games. Warfronts are large-scale, 20-player cooperative PvE scenario confrontations, where the heroes' objective is to claim a key strategic location for their faction. Players build up their faction's forces, lead the charge as their troops lay siege to the objective, and battle enemy commanders as they make their last stand in this epic mode inspired by classic Warcraft RTS battles. Warcraft Legends was a cancelled Warcraft game developed by Blizzard Entertainment, between the release of Warcraft II and III. Legends featured no base building, no fog of war, and used an over-the-shoulder camera as players controlled a single hero. The game was scrapped during development, but the game's hero focus were transitioned over to Warcraft III with an infusion of hefty RPG elements into a real-time strategy game.
